draft.shortGloss: to pay; to hand in; to make or put out
draft.emotion: matter-of-fact and direct, simply stating a cost or an action
notes: 내다 is used in many common expressions where something is put forth or produced, such as 소리를 내다 (to make a sound), 시간을 내다 (to make time), and 용기를 내다 (to muster courage).

senses.definition: To give money for goods, services, or a fee.

examples.translation: I will pay for the meal.

senses.definition: To hand in or submit something, such as homework, a report, or an application.

examples.translation: I have to turn in my homework by tomorrow.

senses.definition: To produce, make, or bring forth something such as a sound, time, or effort.

examples.text: 도서관에서는 큰 소리를 내면 안 돼요.
examples.translation: You must not make loud noises in the library.

faults.why: In Korean you pay money/price (돈/값을 내다) or do the bill (계산하다), not 계산서를 내다.

faults.quote: To cause something to appear or come out from within.
faults.why: Conflates 'submitting/handing in' with 'producing/making (a sound, time, courage)'.
